info.description: The Indices REST API. See docs for details: https://docs.indices.io

post.description:
Spawn a browser session that records the network traffic of everything done in it.

Once completed, the capture session is a reusable recording: attach it to a task to generate an API from it.

get.description:
Retrieve a capture session by its ID.

Poll this after requesting completion: the session is a usable recording once state is completed.

parameters.name: id

schema.description: The ID of the capture session to retrieve.
schema.title: Id

parameters.description: The ID of the capture session to retrieve.

post.description:
Stop recording and finalize the capture session.

Completion is asynchronous: the browser uploads its recording and the session then transitions to completed. Poll retrieveCaptureSession to observe the transition.

parameters.name: id

schema.description: The ID of the capture session to complete.
schema.title: Id

parameters.description: The ID of the capture session to complete.

id.description: Unique identifier for the capture session.

state.description: Current state of the capture session. A session records while active, is completing once completion is requested, and becomes a reusable recording once completed.

browser_session_id.description: Opaque identifier for the spawned browser session. Null once the browser is gone.

iframe_url.description: URL to embed in an iframe to control the browser. Only usable while the session is active.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the object was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the object was last updated.

size_bytes.description: Size of the stored file in bytes, as reported by storage.

content_type.description: MIME type of the stored file.

crc32c.description: Base64-encoded CRC32C checksum reported by storage.

display_name.description: Short human-readable name of the connector.

purpose.description: What the connector does, as specified at publish time.
examples: Retrieve invoices from our ERP system, including refunds.
purpose.example: Retrieve invoices from our ERP system, including refunds.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema for the connector's run arguments.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema for the connector's run results.

required_secrets.description: Secret slots that must be bound when running the connector.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the object was created.

connector_id.description: ID of the connector to execute.

arguments.description: Arguments to pass to the connector. Optional if the connector does not require any arguments.

secret_bindings.description: Mapping of secret slot names to secret IDs. Each slot defined in the connector's required_secrets must be mapped to a user-owned secret.

async.description: When true, return immediately with a pending run; poll retrieveRun for the result.

max_timeout_s.description: Maximum execution time in seconds before the run is timed out.

secret_type.description: Type of secret: 'login' for credentials, 'string' for simple values.

totp_secret.description: Optional TOTP secret (base32 encoded). Only for 'login' type.

id.description: Unique identifier for the deleted connector.

deleted.description: Always true when the file was deleted.

id.description: Unique identifier of the deleted secret.

deleted.description: Whether the secret was successfully deleted.

source.description: How the file came to exist: uploaded by the user or produced by a run.

run_id.description: ID of the run that produced this file. Null for uploaded files.

size_bytes.description: Size of the file in bytes.

crc32c.description: Base64-encoded CRC32C checksum of the file content.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the file was created.

url.description: Short-lived signed URL to download the file bytes directly from storage.

expires_at.description: When the download URL stops being valid.

size_bytes.description: Exact size of the file in bytes. Enforced by the signed upload URL.

content_type.description: MIME type of the file content.

file_id.description: Server-assigned ID of the pending file.

upload_url.description: Signed URL the sandbox must PUT the file bytes to.

upload_headers.description: Headers that must be sent verbatim with the PUT; they are covered by the URL signature.

expires_at.description: When the upload URL stops being valid.

data.description: The connector's full revision history, most recent first. The first entry is the current revision.
Connectors for the requested page, ordered newest first.

has_more.description: Whether more connectors exist after this page.

next_cursor.description: Pass as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page. Null when has_more is false.

has_more.description: Whether more files exist after this page.

next_cursor.description: Pass as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page. Null when has_more is false.

data.description: Runs for the requested page, ordered newest first.

has_more.description: Whether more runs exist after this page.

next_cursor.description: Pass as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page. Null when has_more is false.

display_name.description: Short human-readable name of the connector.

connector_id.description: ID of the connector executed in this run.

arguments.description: Arguments in this run for the connector's input parameters.

secret_bindings.description: Secrets to use for this run. This dict must be a mapping of secret slot names to secret IDs.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the run: `pending`, `running`, `success`, `connector_error`, `timed_out`, `result_too_large`, or `internal_error`. `connector_error` means the connector's code failed (see `error`); `timed_out` and `internal_error` are platform outcomes worth retrying; `result_too_large` is not retryable as-is.

result_json.description: Execution result of the run. In JSON, matching the connector's output schema. Limited to 100MB; results above 100MB will be truncated and result in a `result_too_large` status.

error.description: Why the run failed. Present iff `status` is `connector_error`; for platform failures the status itself is the reason.

has_logs.description: Whether the run has associated logs

created_at.description: Timestamp when the object was created.

finished_at.description: Timestamp when the object was last updated.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the run with the same arguments is expected to succeed. Null when unknown.

exception.description: Exception class name, when the failure came from a raised exception.

details.description: Structured context reported by the connector.

has_totp.description: Whether the secret has a TOTP configured (only applicable for login type).

created_at.description: Timestamp when the secret was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the secret was last updated.

name.description: Name of the secret slot, used as the key in a run's secret_bindings.

supports_totp.description: Whether the connector can perform 2FA/TOTP when the bound login has it configured. Logins without TOTP remain bindable. Only applicable for 'login' type.

description.description: What the bound secret is used for, when the connector declares it.
examples: Amazon account whose orders are fetched.
description.example: Amazon account whose orders are fetched.

http_only.description: Whether the cookie is HTTP only.
